prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1413; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable with that?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the accident in Baytown?

A: I was stopped at a red light on the main road, heading toward the freeway. I had been there for a few seconds when I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped back and then forward.

Q: Were you able to see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?

A: No. I was looking at the light and my mirror, and I didn't see it coming. It was going pretty fast, I think.

Q: Did you get out of your car and speak with the other driver?

A: Yes, we both got out. He said he looked down at his phone for a moment and didn't brake in time. He seemed apologetic.

Q: Did you have any injuries at the scene?

A: I had a stiff neck and some pain across my shoulders, but I figured it would wear off. By that evening it was much worse.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning and then started physical therapy. The doctor diagnosed whiplash and gave me a neck brace for a few weeks.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. I get headaches most days, and turning my head to the left is painful. I've had to take some time off work because sitting at my desk for long periods makes it worse.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident or your injuries?

A: Not that I can think of. I'm just hoping to get back to normal soon.

Q: Thank you for your time. We'll be in touch with next steps.

A: Thanks, I appreciate it.
